title: Infant-directed speech is a finding about infants, not a register for every young person
body: Fernald (1985) is titled 'Four-month-old infants prefer to listen to motherese.' The DOI resolved, and the title is the claim this card uses. The article body was not re-opened, so no effect size, no acoustic recipe, and no age range beyond the title's four months is stated. A preference in four-month-olds is not a reason to speak baby talk to a child who is holding a conversation, and it is not a reason to decide from the voice that the caller is an infant. Year-by-year vocabulary bands are not in this pack.
